checked.claim: Garante fined OpenAI EUR 15m December 2024; Rome Tribunal suspended March 2025, annulled 20 March 2026; Cassazione appeal unknown
checked.evidence: ANSA 20 March 2026: Rome Tribunal annulled the EUR 15m fine imposed on 20 December 2024; the tribunal had suspended it in March 2025. No mention of a Cassazione appeal.

checked.claim: Milan Tribunal business section held admissible VZS representative action for non-material damage from 2018-2019 Facebook scraping; loss of control compensable if actually experienced
checked.evidence: Veltri: Tribunale di Milano, Sez. XIV civile specializzata in materia di impresa, 11 December 2025, VZS v Meta Platforms Ireland; about 533 million users; scraping 2018-2019; loss of control compensable without a seriousness threshold if concrete negative feelings are shown; basis d.lgs. 28/2023, Art. 140-ter Consumer Code, Art. 82 GDPR.

checked.claim: Milan Tribunal 11 December 2025 admissible VZS collective action re 533 million users
checked.evidence: Same source: date, parties and user count match.
Art. 166 sets the Garante's sanctioning procedure (notification, defence, decision).

checked.claim: Public bodies can be fined; no separate cap
checked.evidence: Not checked against a source. It is consistent with the Codice, which sets no separate cap, and with the Garante's routine practice of fining public bodies.

checked.claim: Pay half within the appeal deadline (Art. 166(8)); 50% of revenue reinvested; Art. 167 offences up to 1.5 years, or 1 to 3 years for special categories and transfers
checked.evidence: Art. 166(8): comply and pay 'una somma pari alla metà della sanzione irrogata' before the appeal deadline; Art. 166(7): 50% of annual fine proceeds reassigned to the Garante. Art. 167(1) 'da sei mesi a un anno e sei mesi'; (2) and (3) 'da uno a tre anni'. All require intent to profit or harm and actual harm (nocumento).

checked.claim: Ordinary Tribunale, single judge, where controller based or data subject resides, labour procedure
checked.evidence: Art. 10 d.lgs. 150/2011: labour procedure, 'il tribunale del luogo in cui il titolare del trattamento risiede o ha sede ovvero il tribunale del luogo di residenza dell'interessato'. The single-judge composition was not re-quoted.
Art. 10: 30 days from notification, 60 if resident abroad.

checked.claim: No automatic suspension; judge can suspend (Art. 5 d.lgs. 150/2011); Rome Tribunal suspended OpenAI fine March 2025
checked.evidence: ANSA confirms March 2025 suspension pending judgment. Art. 5 not separately fetched; it is the general suspension rule of d.lgs. 150/2011.

checked.claim: Judgment not appealable on the merits; only Cassazione
checked.evidence: Art. 10: 'La sentenza che definisce il giudizio non è appellabile' (Cassazione remains under Art. 111 Constitution).

checked.claim: Nine months, progress update within three, extendable to twelve (Art. 143)
checked.evidence: Art. 143: decide 'entro nove mesi', inform within three months, twelve months for investigative needs; the time limit is also suspended for the duration of an Art. 60 GDPR cooperation procedure, which the field omits.
checked.replacement: The Garante must decide within nine months of filing and inform the complainant of progress within three months; extendable to twelve months for investigative needs, and suspended while an Art. 60 GDPR cooperation procedure runs (Art. 143 Codice). No time limit for complaining identified.

checked.claim: 30-day written defence and right to a hearing (Art. 166(6))
checked.evidence: Art. 166(6): within thirty days the offender may send written defences and ask to be heard.

checked.claim: Collegio; Art. 166(9) separation of investigative and decision functions
checked.evidence: Art. 166(9) requires rules on separation between investigatory and decision-making functions.

checked.claim: Four members, two per chamber, seven-year non-renewable term; Scorza resigned January 2026; Stanzione, Cerrina Feroni, Ghiglia continue
checked.evidence: Art. 153: 'quattro componenti, eletti due dalla Camera ... e due dal Senato'; 'durata settennale e non sono rinnovabili'. Prima Online 19 Jan 2026: Scorza resigned; President Stanzione, Vice President Cerrina Feroni and Ghiglia said they would continue.

checked.claim: Appeals to the civil Tribunale, no appeal on merits, straight to Cassazione

checked.evidence: Art. 143. (Also suspended during Art. 60 cooperation; see complaint.deadlines.)

checked.claim: Fines already paid reduce the criminal penalty (Art. 167(6))
checked.evidence: Art. 167(6): where the Garante's fine for the same act has been collected, 'la pena è diminuita'.

notes: No errors found in the cases. The only substantive addition: under Art. 143, the nine/twelve-month clock is suspended during Art. 60 cooperation, which matters for cross-border complaints. The plain-language text says 'twelve at most', which is misleading for those cases; consider adding 'unless the case involves other EU regulators'. Art. 167 offences also require actual harm to the data subject, not just intent. Brocardi and Jurinote are secondary sources; the Gazzetta Ufficiale link was not fetched.
